title: Pre-Analysis — Output Bus Bar and Contactor Standard Against the Spares Release
abstract: Closed work order re-examining the direct current bus bar standard before the spares release, checking that the retrofit population and the relay supply position had not moved since the original analysis.

sections.objective: Re-open the pre-analysis of the output bus bar standard for the spares release, three years after the original work order closed. The question was narrower than the first time: not whether the change was right, but whether the relay assembly could be withdrawn from the catalogue at the pre-modification standard without stranding operators who had not yet embodied, and whether the retrofit population had shifted enough to change the kit forecast.
sections.findings_summary: The retrofit population had fallen from three hundred and eighty aircraft to about ninety, faster than the original forecast, which is explained by the bulletin being taken up during unrelated avionics bay work rather than on its own. Two items needed attention. The relay assembly is called out in the trouble shooting procedure for the ground-only unit fault as a possible cause, and withdrawing the pre-modification item from the catalogue would leave that procedure naming a part nobody can buy; the procedure was amended rather than the catalogue held open. The parts figure carries the pre and post modification split correctly but the relay kit and the bus bar are not flagged as a mandatory set, and an operator ordering one without the other would build a configuration that is not approved. The maintenance installation task already carries the terminal torque sequence and needed no change.
sections.next_steps: Amend the trouble shooting procedure so that the pre-modification relay is described rather than called out by part number. Raise an illustrated parts change to flag the bus bar and relay kit as a mandatory set. Release the spares position as planned and hold no further stock of the pre-modification relay beyond the declared last-time-buy.

similarity_seeds: relaxed bolted joint at a direct current terminal
spares withdrawal for a superseded relay assembly

tasks.title: Re-establish the retrofit population from the fleet embodiment record
Check every document that names the pre-modification relay
Confirm the parts figure expresses the mandatory set

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the relay part number, which the procedure names directly in its cause list.

expected_findings.rationale: The trouble shooting procedure names the pre-modification relay assembly by part number as a possible cause. Withdrawing that part from the catalogue leaves the procedure pointing at something an operator cannot obtain.
expected_findings.resolution: Amend the procedure to describe the item rather than name it, effective with the spares withdrawal.

evidence.similarity_note: Reached by traversing from the modification to the figure it replaces parts in.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure carries the pre and post modification split but does not express that the bus bar and the relay kit must be ordered together. An operator ordering one alone would build an unapproved configuration.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise an illustrated parts change to flag the two items as a mandatory set.

evidence.similarity_note: Found through the applicability condition rather than through any shared identifier.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin effectivity is written against the pre-modification population, which has fallen faster than forecast. The stated compliance window now extends beyond the point at which kits will still be produced.
expected_findings.resolution: Restate the compliance time against a fixed date rather than a rolling window, and publish the last kit order date.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. The spares release may proceed subject to the two documentation actions.
